items.title: Phasmophobia Replaced Its Whole VR Character Rig, and Half the VR Fixes Are Doors
items.summary: Kinetic Games did not tune Phasmophobia's VR character rig in v0.19.0.0, it replaced the whole thing and matched the model to your own arm length. Five of the…
items.content:
The character rig is the part of a VR game you stop noticing when it works. It is the skeleton the game hangs on your headset and controllers. It decides where your elbow goes when your hand is here, how far your arm reaches before it stops, and what everyone else in the lobby sees when you crouch behind a sofa. In Phasmophobia v0.19.0.0, which Kinetic Games shipped on August 25, that skeleton is new.

Kinetic said so two weeks ahead of release. From the preview post on August 11: "With this Quality of Life update, we're completely replacing the VR character rig across all platforms. This means more responsive movement in-line with your own body's, improved accuracy on the character model to match player's arm length as well as an overall improvement to visuals of the character model when playing with VR users."

The release notes give all of that one line under Changes: "Improvements have been made to the VR character rig, allowing for more accurate and responsive movement." Read alone, that sounds like tuning. The August post is where the word replacing appears.

Your headset and two controllers give the game three real positions. The rest of your body is inverse kinematics, the engine solving backwards from your hands to a pose that could have produced them. Elbows, shoulders, spine, all of it is a guess. When the model's arms are a fixed length and yours are not, the guess is off in a way you feel before you see it. You reach for a door handle. Your hand arrives near the handle instead of on it.

Matching the model to your own arm length is the correction for that. Kinetic also lists a visual pass on the character model, and that one is for the people watching you rather than for you.

The VR Fixes section runs to ten entries. Half of them are doors.

Opening doors was harder than intended. The reticle, the marker telling you what you are about to grab, displayed wrong when you reached for one. Hand animations broke on tent doors. Doors shoved open with a camera-mounted tripod triggered culling in multiplayer, the rendering shortcut where the engine skips drawing what it thinks you cannot see. A ghost opening a door would push you out of its way.

The other five are the rig showing through. Tripods lagged for other players while you carried them. The Parabolic Microphone's headphones blocked your view. Hands drifted while you walked holding an item. Bodies jittered while crouched in multiplayer. Teleport locomotion refused to work while you held a walkie talkie.

One more sits outside the VR section. Under Player Fixes: hands were moving more slowly than the camera, producing visual lag and stutter. It is filed as a general fix. Hand lag is worse in a headset than on a monitor.

Three entries in the Known Issues list carry a VR label. Head gear can fall off if another player closes a door on you, which makes six. Character profile pictures come up blank when someone joins a lobby. And if Immersive Animations is on when you die, your ragdoll appears distorted and contorted.

The list does not say when any of the three started, and the third is the one to watch. Immersive Animations drives the character model. The character model is what just got replaced. A distorted ragdoll on death is the shape of thing a new rig introduces. Kinetic has not said either way.

There is no separate VR edition. The Steam listing is tagged VR Supported rather than VR Only, so $13.99 buys one game you can run flat or in a headset, tracked controllers either way. On console the VR route is PSVR2 on PS5, patched alongside everything else. Version 0.18.0.0 in July adjusted the PSVR2 player list popup.

Report bugs to the studio rather than the forums. The preview post sends VR players to Kinetic's Help Centre . That reaches the people who rebuilt the rig. A Steam thread does not.

Phasmophobia is number five on our ranking of VR horror games . It is also one of the few flat PC games that ship VR support in the box instead of through a mod, which is why it sits in the built-in section of PCVR Central's catalog .

items.title: Phasmophobia's second Quality of Life update adds Restricted maps, VR fixes, and much creepier deaths
items.summary: Kinetic Games has released Phasmophobia's second Quality of Life update, adding new Restricted maps, VR fixes, and more dramatic ghost hunter deaths.
items.content:
Image credit: Kinetic Games News by Vikki Blake Contributor Published on Aug. 30, 2026, 1:47 p.m. 1 comment Follow Phasmophobia Kinetic Games has released Phasmophobia 's second Quality of Life update, adding a raft of new Restricted maps, streamlined Evidence collection, VR fixes, and considerably more ways to die.

Now live on PC and PlayStation (the Xbox release is "to follow"), the Quality of Life Part 2 update builds on Quality of Life Part 1 which introduced the revamped 13 Willow Street map back in July alongside a batch of other gameplay tweaks.

We're getting a (long-overdue!) set of new small-to-medium Restricted maps for Prison, Brownstone High School, and Point Hope, bringing condensed versions of the original maps designed to speed up investigations and add more variety to runs.

Evidence collection has also been streamlined. Rather than manually checking the in-game journal, players can now tell whether a piece of evidence has already been logged directly from their Photo Camera, Video Camera, or Sound Recorder via faded overlays and yellow LEDs.

Evidence and ghost types selected by teammates will also now show up for the whole team, cutting down on last-minute double-checking before a hunt.

VR players get a more responsive character rig that better tracks real-world body movement, along with a range of community-flagged bug fixes. There are changes to death, too: dying now turns a player's skin greyer and their eyes mistier, and cuts their voice chat the moment they're killed.

The update arrives a couple of months after Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027 , as the studio said it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Update. Kinetic Games ended up apologising to players for issues with its long-awaited 'Player Character Update' , admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".

In numerous patches and hotfixes released since to address the many issues spawned by the latest update, the studio explained how it had been working through player feedback to provide "a much better experience for everyone playing Phasmophobia".

"We've read feedback from across the entire community. The frustration and disappointment has been clear," the team admitted.

items.title: 20 Video Game Secret Areas You Only Have ONE Chance To Discover – Page 13
items.summary: Some video game secrets will not wait for you. You have to find them before they're gone forever! From Baldur's Gate to Pokémon, here are gaming's rarest secret areas.
items.content:
Some secrets will not wait for you. You have to find them before they're gone forever.

Discovering secrets in games can be a lot of fun, and nothing beats the satisfaction of coming across a hidden easter egg or area on your own.

However, you may not realize that some secrets will not just stay around and wait for you to find them. You actually have only one slim chance of stumbling upon them, and if you miss it, they will be gone forever.

Yes, some secret areas are so rare and well-hidden that you can only see them once in your playthrough. They either appear at a specific moment in the game and never again, or their spawn rate is so small that it's statistically improbable to even see them once.

In either case, this obviously makes these secrets quite exclusive, adding to their mysterious allure and severely limiting the number of people who have seen them.

If you want to count yourself among those lucky individuals who have found these secret areas, you can follow this list for useful tips. It may still not guarantee you'll see them, but if you do, you're in for one thrilling discovery.

Cyberpunk 2077’s Night City is fully yours to explore, but some of the quest locations in the game become inaccessible after you finish your business there. One of these locales is the dollhouse called Clouds that you visit to find more information about Evelyn Parker’s mysterious disappearance.

The club management (and the mission objectives) will want you to stay on course and not stray from the designated path, but some exploration is warranted, as there is one hidden room that you can visit here for a special reward that you won’t be able to normally access afterwards.

Given that Clouds is Evelyn’s former workplace, you can actually find the booth where she used to work inside the club. The booth features some of Evelyn’s personal belongings, including a unique katana called the Cocktail Stick.

You only get to access Clouds during one of the main story missions. After the gig is done, Clouds becomes inaccessible, and even if you find a way inside the club with exploits, the entire facility will be empty.

The extra time finding and exploring Evelyn’s room only takes a couple of minutes, and you get to walk away with an awesome-looking weapon, so don’t miss it.

items.title: Phasmophobia devs Kinetic Games mosey into publishing with a witchy delivery game, a parasitic Metroidvania, and more
items.summary: More games than you can shake a stick at!
items.content:
Image credit: Electric Saint News by Oisin Kuhnke Contributor Published on Aug. 13, 2026, 7:01 p.m. 4 comments Follow Aether Wizard Life Kinetic Games are keeping busy! You may have heard yesterday that the Phasmophobia developer is publishing the next game from Her Story and Immortality's Sam Barlow (who's roped in Brandon Cronenberg this time around). That's not all that was announced however, as there's a bevy of other, not even scary at all, actually, games that are coming up from the new publisher.

First up is Crescent County . This one comes from developer Electric Saint, and it's probably the one I'm most personally looking forward to out of the list here. It puts you in the role of a delivery driver, just one set in a world where magic and tech are blended together. Your vehicle of choice is a motorbroom, obviously much sicker than motorbikes (don't bring up Akira, that wouldn't be fair to anyone), and you can also form bonds - or flirt - with a range of characters you meet on your delivery runs.

Then there's Shellbound , a Metroidvania that went to the Hollow Knight school of graphics most certainly. In this one you're a parasite that can control its enemies travelling around the inside of a giant snail, presenting a concoction of flesh and machinery that disgusts and delights in equal parts. I'm quite intrigued by the fact that killing too much of a given enemy species will slowly let them evolve into something stronger, providing both a greater challenge and strength if you take them over.

Up next is Contact Protocol , certainly one for retrofuturism and Alien fans. You play as a security officer aboard a corporate spaceship ferrying miners towards Jupiter's biggest moon, Ganymede. It's up to you to "assess the intentions of approaching ships, decide their fate, and keep your crew alive." And of course, "the company is watching."

Lastly, there's Aether Wizard Life , another magicy entry that gives off some light Spiritfarer vibes. Here you're a young apprentice mage who resides in a haunted town, learning a bunch of spells, brewing potions, crafting weapons and the like, all the while building up your very own castle.

It's an interesting slate from Kinetic Games, or I should say Kinetic Publishing. Mostly what I'm taken aback by is the fact that we have an indie studio here that has found a lot of success, and is sharing that with other devs and games that don't fit into that vaguely shaped mould of "instant viral hit." While not exactly the same, it reminds me of Among Us developer Innersloth's Outersloth , a fund for independent game devs. Among Us obviously continues to find success many years after the pandemic first took hold, and Outersloth continue to put out more games they've helped to fund. At a time when the industry is [choose whatever metaphor feels most appropriate to you, dear read], seeing indies express even the smallest amount of solidarity like this is a little heartwarming at the very least. May it continue!

Welcome back, Ghost Hunters.

Thank you to everyone for the warm reception to our first Quality of Life update last month, and we’re glad to see many of you enjoying Phasmophobia once more.

Today as promised, we’re sharing details on the upcoming second Quality of Life update for Phasmophobia. We’ll be releasing this update across all platforms on 25th August, 2026. Exact release times are still to be confirmed, so keep an eye on our channels for official confirmation of when the update is live. 

Let’s break down a couple of the features we’re excited about before sharing the full list: 

New Restricted Options

For a long while, we have seen folks requesting smaller versions of our larger maps in the vein of Sunny Meadows Restricted. With this update we’re excited to introduce Restricted versions for Prison, Brownstone High School and Point Hope.

As with Sunny Meadows, these map variants are designed for quicker games in locations that we know players enjoy but sometimes don’t want to be investigating the larger area. In the case of Point Hope Restricted, which will be classed as small, Ghost Hunters will be able to access up to the Dining Room while Prison and Brownstone High School will have multiple variants - classed as Small and Medium respectively - which will be randomly assigned upon loading into a contract. 

Brownstone High School in particular will have a total of 4 map variants following the update. With such a big map, we believed it was appropriate to give a variety of variations, giving Ghost Hunters a sense of mystery when loading up. Outside each Restricted version of the map, a small piece of environmental decor will signify which variant of the map you’re on.

Journal & Evidence Changes

We made a handful of changes and improvements to Evidence collection with the first Quality of Life update, and we’re doing the same with the second. As with all of our updates, we’ll be looking for and reading through player feedback on these changes so please do let us know your thoughts once you’ve spent some time with them. 

Since our Chronicle update last year, we’ve been working on finessing the Unique/Duplicate system. A change we’re introducing with this next update means there’ll now be visual indicators to show that a piece of Media a Ghost Hunter captures is a Duplicate without the need to check the Journal. 

To detect a Duplicate, keep an eye out for the following indicators:

  • Tier 1 Photo Cameras will display a yellow LED light.

    [/*]

  • Tier 2 & 3 Photo Cameras and all Tiers of Video Cameras will display a faded overlay, rather than the usual bold white text.

  • Tier 1 Sound Recorder will lower the brightness of the Volume indicators.

  • Tier 2 & 3 Sound Recorders will display faded sound waves.

    [/*]

Another important addition in this update is being able to see other Ghost Hunters’ Evidence and Ghost selections in the Journal. This means there’ll be no more need to double check with other players which pieces of Evidence you’ve captured and see other’s opinions on which Ghost the group is dealing with - and of course making sure everyone has the same selection when you’re leaving in the Truck!

Elsewhere, we’ve replaced the Keys section in the journal with the ‘Items We’ve Found’ section. Appearing in the order they are found, this will display collected items such as keys, the bone and seasonal event collectables. On this same page, a gender symbol (♀/♂) will now be displayed alongside the Ghost's name, allowing for easier understanding of male and female names and Ghost types - especially for non-English speaking players.

VR Improvements

With this Quality of Life update, we’re completely replacing the VR character rig across all platforms. This means more responsive movement in-line with your own body’s, improved accuracy on the character model to match player’s arm length as well as an overall improvement to visuals of the character model when playing with VR users.

We’re also addressing several regularly reported issues from VR players, which we’ll detail in the full patch notes at release. As with other areas of Phasmophobia, please do let us know any feedback you have from your time in VR or any issues you encounter via our Help Centre.

Gameplay Improvements

Finally, for today, we just wanted to dive in to some of the changes coming to the gameplay of Phasmophobia. Firstly, we’ll be implementing the ability to select the Ghost Type for any Custom Difficulty investigations. You’ll find this in the Ghost settings when setting up your game, as you can see in the screenshot below.

Another change with this update is a change to character appearance upon death. As seen below, the dead body will now be seen with a greyer skin as well as misty eyes. Dead players will also appear this way to others while Dead. In addition to this change a player’s voice chat will now be cut off as soon as they die - the moment their neck is snapped during the death animation.

Below, you’ll find a list of all the New features coming with this Quality of Life update as well as the Changes section. At the release of the update, as mentioned, we’ll share the full patch notes along with the list of Fixes for known bugs and issues. We look forward to sharing this update with you on August 25th, 2026.

The New

As part of the Quality of Life update, we’re introducing a handful of new gameplay features that aim to improve the overall experience of playing Phasmophobia. 

Read the below for some details on these additions.

      [/*]

    • Improvements to crouching.

      [/*]

      [/*]

    • Held items will no longer sway when walking.

      [/*]

    • The character's position will accurately represent your real life body position.

      [/*]
    [/*]

13 Willow Street

As with all our reworked maps, 13 Willow Street will retain its overall original layout with a few minor changes. The core of these reworks has always been bringing the visuals up to our standards while letting each location speak for itself. As much as we love the original versions of these maps, giving them their own identities and stories has been something we’ve always wanted to achieve and we’re excited that we’ve been able to. 

Following 6 Tanglewood Drive, we know that 13 Willow Street holds a special place in a Ghost Hunter’s heart. We’ve kept that at the forefront while developing the rework, making sure that those first few steps inside feel new but familiar, and entice you to explore during each and every contract.

Check out the screenshots below for a look inside 13 Willow Street.

13 Willow Street will launch alongside the Quality of Life update on July 21st, 2026 for all platforms. Stay tuned to our social channels and our official Discord server for exact release timings. As is tradition with a new map, a new ID Card and Badge will be available upon completion of the map’s challenge. By correctly identifying 50 ghosts (and surviving) Ghost Hunters will earn the Sun Seeker set, as seen below.

We’ll also be running a new Twitch Drops campaign for the first week after launch. Players will be able to earn the animated and static versions of the Cool Cat ID Card and Badge between 21st July - 28th July by watching a total of 2 hours of Phasmophobia streams.

The animated version will be exclusively available via Kinetic Games Partner channels.

We’re looking forward to getting this update out to you next week and will be keeping an eye on every bit of feedback sent to us on social, in Discord or otherwise.

items.content:
Welcome back, Ghost Hunters. 

Over the last month and a half, we’ve been reading the discussions about Phasmophobia across so many different channels and taking note of the biggest issues, points of concern, questions and more. We are sorry it’s taken a while to respond, but we wanted to make sure that when we did, we had something of substance for you. Hopefully today, with our updated Roadmap and information on what’s to come to Phasmophobia, we can start to build back your trust and have meaningful conversations around the game we all care so deeply about.

We’ll go in to more detail on everything in this blog, but for those of you that would rather just have the headlines, here we go:

  • The rework of 13 Willow Street will launch July 21st, 2026 alongside a Quality of Life update.

    [/*]

  • A further Quality of Life update will launch in August 2026.

    [/*]

  • Our  upgrade to Unity 6 will take place in October 2026.

    [/*]

  • An additional Player Character update will launch in November, bringing with it improved animations, character models, UI, more clothing and customisation options.

    [/*]

  • Phasmophobia 1.0, as well as our next new map, will now launch in 2027.

    [/*]

A New Roadmap

Over the last month, we’ve taken a look at our plans for 2026 and made important decisions and changes to make sure we get things right. Phasmophobia’s new Roadmap, which can be seen below, focuses on bringing the game back in-line with our vision and one that we hope reignites your passion for it. 

With a focus on quality of life over new content, our various updates will bring with them hundreds of fixes - starting with our first update in July - as well as bringing the game up- to-date with Unity 6. Our second Player Character update will improve and redo areas such as the animations, character models, UI and introduce a host of new customisation options.

Alongside these various updates, you can expect to see more regular Development Previews that’ll take you deeper into what they’ll contain and the improvements they’ll bring to Phasmophobia.

You may notice that a few things have been removed from the Roadmap for 2026, such as Phasmophobia 1.0 and our new map. While we’ll talk more about the 1.0 delay further down in this blog, we want to reassure you that a new map will be coming to Phasmophobia, just a little later than planned.

For now, let’s go into a little detail on the first update - bringing with it the reworked 13 Willow Street. Willow Update

Our 13 Willow Street Rework update will launch on 21st July, 2026, bringing with it the reworked map and the first of our Quality of Life updates.

Before we get into the second part, let’s take a look at the new 13 Willow Street.

As with our rework on 6 Tanglewood Drive, this new version of 13 Willow Street retains an almost identical layout to the location currently in-game but features redesigned rooms, new theming and plenty of new interactions and objects to discover. 13 Willow Street will continue our approach to storytelling in Phasmophobia too, with a story waiting to be pieced together. We can’t wait to hear your theories and thoughts.

Quality of Life Updates Our Quality of Life updates this year will focus on bug fixes, gameplay improvements and the overall stability and playability of the game. Due to the hundreds of bug fixes, changes and new features currently planned for release, we will be releasing two separate Quality of Life updates - the first with the Willow launch and the second in August 2026. 

These updates have been built off the back of the feedback we’ve received since the launch of the Player Character Update, as well as changes we’ve wanted to implement for a long time. We’ll provide full patch notes and details at release of the updates, but here’s a few details on some of the improvements: 

  • New keybinds for pressing 1,2,3 and 4 for the individual inventory slots for keyboard and mouse only.

    [/*]

  • FOV adjustments for held items to increase item visibility.

    [/*]

  • Eye Adaptation option for console players.

    [/*]

  • Moving the Truck closer to map entrances on Prison and Brownstone High School.

    [/*]

  • Restricted map variants for Point Hope, Brownstone High School and Prison.

    [/*]

  • VR improvements; equipment usability changes, belt improvements, character movement and more.

    [/*]

  • The legacy badge screen will be available in the customisation shop to allow you to customise it whenever you want to.

    [/*]

  • The collected bone will show in the Journal.

    [/*]

  • The ghost type can be selected as a custom difficulty option.

    [/*]

  • The zoom feature in the Customisation Shop will now zoom in on the selected area.

    [/*]

  • Ability to raise the Watch while carrying equipment.

    [/*]

  • Improvements to character animations; leg movements, appearance changes when dead.

    [/*]

  • Equipment switching animation speed increases including making opening and closing the journal almost instant.

    [/*]

  • Improvements to photo detection as well as showing an indicator for what you are taking a photo of, similar to video cameras.

    [/*]

  • Equipment can be instantly used, allowing the animation to be skipped.

    [/*]

These two Quality of Life updates will address most of the issues players are encountering, and aim for them to drastically improve the state of Phasmophobia. Other planned updates, such as our move to Unity 6 later in the year, will further improve the stability and performance of the game.

Phasmophobia 1.0 Launches 2027

Earlier this year, we committed to launching Phasmophobia 1.0 at the end of 2026. Now, following a review of our plans and internal processes, we’re making the decision to move the release of 1.0 to the second half of 2027. The game will be coming to the Nintendo Switch 2 at the same time too.

We know this will come as a disappointment to many, but this is the right decision to ensure we deliver the 1.0 version of Phasmophobia that is true to our vision, high quality standards and provides the experience for players that we’ve always wanted to achieve.

We’re not going to stay quiet though. Beginning in 2027 we’ll be bringing you with us during development through regular streams and other means; showcasing our work, sharing some of the secrets of Phasmophobia 1.0 and much more. While we won’t spoil all of the surprises, we want to be as visible as possible for you, hopefully rebuilding the trust that we’ve understandably lost this year.

That said, let’s not wait until the new year to share something.

Below is our first look at the improved model for Patient 07, a fan-favourite who - along with all of our ghost models - is getting a much needed glow up in 1.0.

All of our ghost models will be given a new lease of life(?) with this visual upgrade, but will also be providing their own unique experiences for players. What that entails exactly is something we’ll go into more detail with down the line, but we look forward to sharing that with you when we’re ready to.

Another aspect of 1.0 we want to reveal today is the introduction of Conduits. Replacing the Bone as a collectable during each contract, these are unique items paired with a particular ghost model. 

A Conduit is an item that ties a ghost to our world, preventing them from moving on. These items will provide new lore to the ghost and the overall world of Phasmophobia.

Perhaps you can piece together some tidbits already? 

Rest of the Year

We’ve focused on some of this year’s major updates for Phasmophobia, but as you can see, the Roadmap features more than just these. Following on from our two Quality of Life updates, we’ll be making the jump up to Unity 6 in October. 

This Unity 6 update will provide some crucial stability updates as well as a brand new lighting system for Phasmophobia. We’ll also be implementing further accessibility options such as preferences for colour blind players as well as further quality of life improvements and bug fixes. We’ll dive deeper into these changes in a Development Preview later this year, so please do keep an eye out for that. 

Our second Player Character update will arrive in November, bringing with it brand new customisation options and cosmetics, an improved Shop UI as well as new animations and graphical improvements for our character models in-game, giving each character much more life and personality than is currently available. 

Elsewhere, we’ll see the return of Crimson Eye and Winter’s Jest (sans leaderboards) as well as our third map rework of the year, 42 Edgefield Road. Finally, we’re also planning one extra content update for the game later in 2026 that’ll bring with it changes to our Weekly Challenges ,new Voice Recognition features and more. We will share details on all of our updates when the time is right.

Moving Phasmophobia 1.0 to 2027 allows us the time and resources to get it to the high standard that you all deserve and to rebuild the relationship between Kinetic Games and you, our community. While the news of delays is never a good thing, we do hope that the information we’ve shared with you today helps you understand our decision.

We’re sorry for how Phasmophobia was left following our last update, and we understand your frustration. The Player Character Update did not meet the standards we set for ourselves or the expectations you have for the game. Our next update is the first step in a new direction, and we look forward to sharing it with you on July 21st.

Thank you, Ghost Hunters, for your time reading this blog, your passion and support for Phasmophobia and so much more.

Welcome back, Ghost Hunters.

Today we have released our latest update for Phasmophobia, addressing several known issues in the game.

We are aware of the current ongoing issues in-game and are currently implementing fixes and improvements in future updates for Phasmophobia. We’ll be sharing our plans for the rest of 2026 later this month with you all, including a timeline for fixes and updates related to both the Player Character Update and game in general. In the meantime, please continue to provide feedback and bug reports so that our team can investigate as much as possible. You can submit any and all issues via our Support Centre.

New

  • The VR belt has been reimplemented following player feedback. Players will now also be able to switch between having their Journal and Walkie Talkie on the belt or their shoulder. 

    • The VR belt will only be visible locally, players who are looking at a VR player will see the equipment on their body instead.

      [/*]
    [/*]

Changes

  • The line of sight ghost speed accelerations implemented in the Player Character Update have been reverted to their original state.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Fixed an issue that caused players to become softlocked when using the Spirit Box before interacting with the Truck’s CCTV.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue that allowed the Kormos to kill players through floors.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue that allowed the Kormos to kill players outside.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue that caused the Tier 3 Firelight to not work correctly if placed while lit.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where player jackets would appear incorrectly when loading into a Multiplayer lobby.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where pressing ‘Join’ in Multiplayer without having a code entered would cause issues creating lobbies, and remove audio from the game.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where VR players were unable to use Text Input for the Spirit Box, Monkey Paw and Ouija Board.

    [/*]

Known Issues

  • Players across all platforms are experiencing issues with voice recognition/voice chat. A fix is being investigated.

    [/*]

Please note: Following this update, players on Windows 7/8 or other out-of-date Windows installs may need to run Windows Update (and restart) for voice chat to connect. This is due to a recent security certificate update on our voice servers. More info can be found here.

As you continue your investigations in Phasmophobia, if you encounter bugs, issues or simply have feedback for our team, please use our Support Centre to submit your reports.
